reasoning: Both are valid, mergeable answers with a shared reactive module and a single UIScale. B handles touch placement more robustly: it computes the strip between the thumbstick and jump button, shrinks tiles to fit (never below 44) and wraps them, picks the touch layout from screen size as well as input, and tracks the topbar inset. A's top-centre row is reasonable but can overflow narrow phones, and its layout ignores screen size.

criteria.note: UI/Responsive.luau holds viewportSize and inputMode (from PreferredInput) as Vide sources, re-hooking on CurrentCamera and ViewportSize changes; it has no topbar inset source and relies on ScreenInsets instead.
Screen.luau binds a single UIScale to Responsive.scale, which is the short side / 1080 clamped between 1 and 4 on desktop.

criteria.criterion: 3. Small screens change layout, not shrink
criteria.note: Scale is clamped to at least 1; touch switches to a horizontal row of 48-unit tiles with no names, but the row never wraps and could overflow a narrow portrait phone.
isTouch comes from PreferredInput (not TouchEnabled), but screen size never drives the layout, so a tiny desktop window keeps the column.

criteria.criterion: 5. Clear of thumbstick, jump button, and topbar
criteria.note: The touch row is anchored top-centre 8 units from the top inside CoreUISafeInsets, so it avoids the lower-left and lower-right controls and sits below the topbar; the placement is simple rather than computed.

criteria.criterion: 6. Text keeps up with the scale
criteria.note: Replaced TextScaled and the UITextSizeConstraint with a fixed TextSize = 22, so the title grows with the UIScale.
Every changing property is bound, there is no nested scope, LayoutOrder is fixed, and all checks pass; ScaledSize strokes keep the outline proportional.
Screen.luau keeps the viewport, topbar inset, PreferredInput, and ViewportDisplaySize as sources, updated in one batch from the camera, TopbarInset, and PreferredInput signals.
GameScreenGui binds a single UIScale to Screen.uiScale (short side / 1080, clamped 1 to 3).

criteria.criterion: 3. Small screens change layout, not shrink
criteria.note: Minimum scale is 1; the Row layout fits tiles to MaxWidth, clamped to at least 44, and wraps with a UIGridLayout.
isTouchLayout = prefersTouch() or isPhone(), so it uses both primary input and screen size.

criteria.criterion: 5. Clear of thumbstick, jump button, and topbar
criteria.note: bottomBand starts right of the 40%-width thumbstick region and stops left of the jump button (sized for small or large screens); the row is centred in that band at the bottom, well below the topbar.

criteria.criterion: 6. Text keeps up with the scale
criteria.note: The title uses a fixed TextSize from the metrics; the constraint is removed.
derive is used at component scope, all props are bound, Active sinks stray taps, and all checks pass.

strengths: Clean, reusable Responsive and Screen modules, with a README section for future screens
Uses PreferredInput, gamepad scale boost, and safe insets
Fixed TextSize so text scales with the UIScale
weaknesses: The touch row doesn't wrap and could overflow narrow phones
Layout ignores screen size, so a tiny desktop window keeps the column
No topbar inset in the shared state

strengths: Computed band between the touch controls, with tile fitting and wrapping
Touch layout picked from both input and screen size
Thorough shared Screen module including the topbar inset, plus a GameScreenGui root for future screens
weaknesses: More complex, with hardcoded jump-button offsets copied from the PlayerModule
Desktop tile size changed from 40 to 44 without being asked
